newsitem.title: UK: Nordic American says tanker rates start above base.
newsitem.headline: Nordic American says tanker rates start above base.

text.p: Nordic American Tanker Shipping said Wednesday that tanker freight rates for its first tanker are set to start above the base rate of its contract with British Petroleum Co Plc.
That promises to offer warrant holders in the special purpose tanker firm a premium on the guaranteed minimum dividend.
Nordic American said it will formally take delivery of the 150,000dwt suezmax crude tanker British Harrier on August 4. It is the first of three vessels being built for the company.
Freight rates for the vessel calculated by Clarkson Research Studies in London are currently above the $22,000 per day base rate agreed with BP, Nordic American said.
Herbjorn Hansson, president of Ugland Nordic Shipping the parent of Nordic American, said rates are running at $23,000 to $25,000 per day at present.

BP has guaranteed to pay Nordic American a minimum bareboat rate of $13,500 for seven years -- equivalent to a time charter rate of around $22,000. BP has an option to charter the ships for up to a further seven years.
The minimum rate guarantees Nordic American shareholders gain a yield of at least 8 percent on their investment.
Spot tanker rates have risen sharply over the past year. Higher rates will flow through to increased dividends to shareholders.
Nordic American was launched in 1995 as a vehicle for BP to build new tankers without having to fund them through its own balance sheet.
Investors paid a total of $58.7 million for Nordic American warrants. The cash was used to make down payments on three newbuildings at Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd in South Korea.

Warrant holders will be able to exercise their right to convert the warrants into shares this September at $10.21 each. This will raise a further $119.8 million to be used to meet delivery payments on the three ships.
Hansson said Wednesday: "We are very bullish about the tanker market, and we expect that the improvement in the markets will benefit Nordic American shares."
Shareholders in Nordic American Shipping voted to change its name to Ugland Nordic Shipping in April following the accumulation of a 42 percent stake in the group by Norway's Ugland shipping family.
Ugland Nordic, which currently controls a fleet of 12 tankers, will report interim results on August 5.
